fields.ic_name: AMBA AXI / ACE Protocol Specification (ARM IHI 0022E)
fields.supersedes: ARM IHI 0022D (28 October 2011); ARM IHI 0022D-2c (03 June 2011 beta) — first inclusion of ACE

First release of AXI specification v2.0

protocol_variants_described: ACE-Lite (AMBA 4) — coherent reads/writes without local cache
fields.purpose: Defines AMBA AXI3, AXI4, AXI4-Lite on-chip bus protocols, plus the AXI Coherency Extensions (ACE and ACE-Lite). ACE adds hardware cache-coherency on top of AXI4 for multi-master systems with caches; ACE-Lite adds coherent reads/writes for non-cached IOs (DMA / GPU / IO accelerators). Provides a complete coherency framework: shareability domains, snoop transactions, distributed virtual memory (DVM) messages, and barrier transactions.
key_features_axi_baseline: Unaligned data transfers via byte strobes
Burst-based transactions with only start address issued
Separate read and write data channels (low-cost DMA)
Easy register stage addition for timing closure
Backward compatible with AHB and APB
key_features_ace_extensions: Hardware cache-coherency via snoop transactions — no software flushes needed for shared regions
Three new snoop channels: AC (Snoop Address), CR (Snoop Response), CD (Snoop Data)
5-state cache-line coherency model: UniqueClean (UC), UniqueDirty (UD), SharedClean (SC), SharedDirty (SD), Invalid (I)
AxDOMAIN[1:0] — Non-shareable / Inner Shareable / Outer Shareable / System shareability domains

AxSNOOP — encodes coherent transaction types (ReadOnce / ReadShared / ReadClean / ReadNotSharedDirty / ReadUnique / CleanUnique / MakeUnique / CleanShared / CleanInvalid / MakeInvalid / WriteUnique / WriteLineUnique / WriteBack / WriteClean / Evict / DVM)
AxBAR — barrier transaction encoding (Normal / Memory / Synchronization / SystemBarrier)
Extended RRESP[3:0] — RRESP[2] PassDirty bit (cache line dirty wrt memory), RRESP[3] IsShared bit (another cache holds copy)
Extended BRESP[2] — DataTransfer indicator for pass-dirty
RACK / WACK acknowledge signals (master to interconnect) — confirms snoop ordering
Distributed Virtual Memory (DVM) — TLB invalidate, branch predictor invalidate, ICache invalidate, virtual address synchronization via the AC channel
Snoop Response: DataTransfer / Error / PassDirty / IsShared / WasUnique bits in CRRESP[4:0]
ACE-Lite subset for non-cached masters that need to issue coherent reads/writes without owning a local cache

cache_line_states_5state.UC_UniqueClean: Only this cache holds a copy; same as main memory.
cache_line_states_5state.UD_UniqueDirty: Only this cache holds a copy; differs from main memory; this cache is responsible for write-back.
cache_line_states_5state.SC_SharedClean: Other caches may hold a copy; same as main memory.
cache_line_states_5state.SD_SharedDirty: Other caches may hold a copy; differs from main memory; this cache is responsible for write-back.
cache_line_states_5state.I_Invalid: This cache does not hold a valid copy.

fields.burst_boundary_rule: A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary (inherited from AXI).
fields.intended_audience: Hardware and software engineers familiar with AMBA AXI3/AXI4 who design coherent multi-master systems, processor clusters, accelerators, or IO bridges.
fields.vendor: Arm Limited, Company 02557590 registered in England, 110 Fulbourn Road, Cambridge, England CB1 9NJ
fields.package_info_rationale: AXI/ACE is a bus protocol specification, not a packaged IC. No package/pinout/electrical-DC data exists in this document.
fields.electrical_specs_rationale: Protocol spec defines only logical signal semantics (synchronous, sampled on rising edge of ACLK, ARESETn active-LOW). No voltage/current/IO-standard information.

evidence.spec_section: C1 ACE Protocol Specification / About the ACE protocol
evidence.quote: The ACE protocol provides hardware cache coherency support and is an extension of the AXI4 protocol.

Each address channel has its own shareability domain signal — ARDOMAIN, AWDOMAIN. The ACE protocol specifies four levels of shareability domain: Non-shareable, Inner Shareable, Outer Shareable, System.

evidence.spec_section: C3.1.1 Shareability domain types / Table C3-2
evidence.quote: AxDOMAIN[1:0]: 0b00 Non-shareable, 0b01 Inner Shareable, 0b10 Outer Shareable, 0b11 System.

evidence.spec_section: C3.1.2 Read and write barrier transactions / Table C3-5
evidence.quote: AxBAR encodes barrier transactions on AR and AW channels.

evidence.spec_section: C3.1.3 Read and write Shareable transaction types / Tables C3-7, C3-8
evidence.quote: Permitted ARBAR[0]/ARDOMAIN/ARSNOOP combinations: ReadNoSnoop, ReadOnce, ReadShared, ReadClean, ReadNotSharedDirty, ReadUnique, CleanUnique, MakeUnique, CleanShared, CleanInvalid, MakeInvalid, Barrier, DVM Complete, DVM Message. AWBAR/AWDOMAIN/AWSNOOP: WriteNoSnoop, WriteUnique, WriteLineUnique, WriteClean, WriteBack, Evict, WriteEvict, Barrier.
RRESP[2] PassDirty bit — cache line is dirty wrt main memory, initiating master must ensure write-back. RRESP[3] IsShared bit — another copy of the data might be held in another cache.

evidence.spec_section: C3.7 Snoop response channel signaling / Table C3-22
evidence.quote: CRRESP[4:0]: [0] DataTransfer, [1] Error, [2] PassDirty, [3] IsShared, [4] WasUnique.
The snoop data bus, CDDATA, is not required to be the same width as the read data and write data buses. The snoop data bus can be 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, or 1024 bits wide.

evidence.spec_section: C5.2 General requirements for snoop transactions / Table C5-4
evidence.quote: Cache line state abbreviations: UC UniqueClean. UD UniqueDirty. SC SharedClean. SD SharedDirty. I Invalid.
